question: An email says CRA needs my bank details through a link to send my refund. Should I use it?
generated_answer:
You should not use the link provided in the email to submit your bank details. This is likely a phishing scam, where fraudsters try to trick people into giving away their personal information, such as bank details or passwords, under false pretenses. The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) will never ask you to click on a link in an email or text message to receive a refund or to confirm your identity or personal information.

Here are some tips to help you identify and avoid phishing scams:

- The CRA will never ask you to provide personal or financial information through an unsolicited email or text message.
- The CRA will never ask you to click on a link to access or confirm your personal information.
- If you receive an email or text message claiming to be from the CRA and asking for your personal or financial information, do not respond. Instead, report it to the CRA by forwarding the suspicious email to  or calling the CRA at 1-800-959-8281.

If you are expecting a refund from the CRA, you can check the status of your refund through your CRA account online or by calling the CRA. You can also use the CRA’s My Account service to securely access and manage your tax and benefit information.

To protect yourself from phishing scams:

- Be cautious of emails or text messages that ask for personal or financial information.
- Never click on links or download attachments in emails or text messages unless you are certain they are from a trusted source.
- Use strong, unique passwords for all your online accounts and enable two-factor authentication where possible.
- Keep your computer and mobile devices up to date with the latest security patches and antivirus software.
- If you believe you have provided personal or financial information to a fraudster, report it to your bank and credit card companies immediately and monitor your accounts closely for any suspicious activity.

Remember, the CRA will never ask you to provide personal or financial information through an unsolicited email or text message. If you have any doubts about the authenticity of an email or text message claiming to be from the CRA, contact the CRA directly through official channels.
